## Statement

An emulation makes many defensible decisions: active comparator, washout period, time zero, grace period, how treatment episodes are constructed, censoring rules, follow-up length and outcome definition. Each has more than one reasonable answer, and the set of answers is the researcher's degrees of freedom. Design guidance now exists and states plainly that the operational methods remain scenario dependent, which means the guidance narrows the set without closing it. Registrations, where they exist, record only the specification that was finally run; they do not record the alternatives considered, the order in which decisions were made, or which decisions were revised after the data were inspected. A reader therefore cannot distinguish a protocol written once from one converged upon.

## Why it is open

The information that would settle it is destroyed rather than merely unrecorded: once a decision log is not kept, no later audit can reconstruct it, and there is no artifact to demand. Registration systems were designed for randomized trials, where the protocol precedes the data, and have no natural slot for a design that is necessarily developed against an existing dataset. Requiring a full multiverse imposes a cost proportional to the number of decisions, which for a longitudinal emulation is large, so the honest practice is also the expensive one.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Hansford HJ, et al. Design and implementation of observational studies emulating a target trial. JAMA Netw Open 2026](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.58262) | Sets out the design decisions and acknowledges that operational methods remain scenario dependent, which is the residual this problem names. |
| [Hansford HJ, Cashin AG, Jones MD, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2025.13350) | A 21-item checklist covering what the study did. It reports the final specification and is explicitly a reporting rather than a design instrument. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Require version-controlled protocols, dated decision logs and outcome-blinded feasibility reports, so that the chronology of decisions is an artifact rather than a memory. Prespecify a primary emulation plus a principled design multiverse over the decisions known to move estimates, and report the distribution rather than the chosen point. Hash the executable specification before outcome analysis, which makes the claim of prespecification checkable by a third party instead of taken on trust.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 3 findings from 3 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed. A further 15 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.

**Dissent.** literature dissented (supported): Nothing in the corpus records a decision log, a dated chronology of design choices, or the alternatives rejected during protocol development. [...]

**Revised by the full-text reading.** Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed
:   **confirmed-open -> partially-addressed** 3 surviving findings from: Illustrating an Adaptive Prespecification Framework for Obse; Improving the validity of noninterventional comparative effe; Transparency in real-world evidence (RWE) studies to build c. New citations: 10.1093/aje/kwae317, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001901, 10.1111/dom.13918

4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **open / supported.** Nothing in the corpus records a decision log, a dated chronology of design choices, or the alternatives rejected during protocol development. Quality-assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies, and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology, evaluate the specification that was published rather than the process that produced it. The entry's claim is about an artifact nobody keeps, which is consistent with its absence from a literature search: the evidence for it is the absence of any paper reporting one.
    Cites 10.1016/s1473-3099(26)00058-7: An appraisal instrument for exactly these studies, which assesses the reported design and not the chronology by which it was reached..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** A final, unversioned protocol cannot reveal unlogged alternatives or their chronology, so an auditability gap can remain. However, this is primarily a governance and implementation problem rather than an unsolved inferential method. Prospective version control, amendment records, decision logs, and trusted timestamps can preserve the history directly. The categorical assertion that registrations retain only the final protocol is not established by technical reasoning, and an unlogged history is unavailable to an auditor but not necessarily destroyed. A full multiverse is neither required for provenance nor automatically interpretable: changing populations, comparators, strategies, or outcomes creates different estimands, so their estimates do not constitute an uncertainty distribution for one parameter. A hash establishes integrity only when paired with a trusted timestamp and does not prove that no alternative analysis existed. This is a roadmap and reporting-standard item rather than a high-severity statistical gap.

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **open / supported.** Registrations and TARGET record the final specification. Multiverse/specification-curve methods (e.g. Simonsohn et al.) and some observational-study preregistration guidance exist, but EU PAS / ClinicalTrials-style registries and TARGET do not require rejected alternatives, decision chronology, or outcome-blinded feasibility logs as first-class artifacts. Version-controlled hashed executable specs before outcome analysis are not standard. Cost of full multiverse remains unsolved. Open as stated.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens
:   **open / supported.** The claim is coherent and proportionate. It states that registrations record only the final specification and not the alternatives considered or the chronology of decisions. The reason given—that registration systems were designed for randomized trials where the protocol precedes the data and have no natural slot for a design developed against an existing dataset—directly entails that the artifact required to settle the issue is not currently produced or demanded by these systems.

Decision path
:   `R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)`

:::

## How the evidence falls in time

18 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2020 to 2026. Partial progress is on the record, and later work still calls this open. Both belong in view.

It is also being **closed in pieces**: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.
